r: Senator-members of the SET cannot all be disqualified even when a contest names all of them; the Constitution intends the judicial and legislative members to decide together, and the three Justices alone cannot adjudicate. Individual members may inhibit as conscience dictates.
f: Losing candidates contested the election of 22 senators, including the six senator-members of the SET, and moved to disqualify them.
h: Motion to disqualify all six denied.
x: Tribunal composition and the ‘necessity’ of senators sitting in judgment of colleagues.

r: Members of an electoral tribunal enjoy security of tenure. The House cannot remove a member for disloyalty to his party or for voting against its candidate; valid causes are expiration of term, death or disability, resignation from or formal change of party, or removal for other valid cause. ‘Sole judge’ means the tribunal is independent of its chamber.
f: After Rep. Camasura voted for Bondoc (the opposing party’s candidate) in the HRET, his party expelled him and the House withdrew his HRET seat on the eve of the decision.
h: Camasura’s removal was void; he was reinstated so the decision could be promulgated.
x: Any attempt by a chamber or party to reshuffle tribunal members to change the outcome of a case.

r: The HRET’s jurisdiction begins only when three things concur: a valid proclamation, a proper oath (before the Speaker in open session), and assumption of office. Until then, COMELEC keeps jurisdiction over a winner’s qualifications.
f: COMELEC cancelled Regina Reyes’s COC for misrepresenting her citizenship and residence; she was proclaimed and took her oath before the Speaker outside session before June 30.
h: COMELEC retained jurisdiction; its cancellation stood.
x: Forum questions: COMELEC or HRET? Check proclamation, oath and assumption.

r: Where the validity of the proclamation itself is pending before COMELEC (a timely motion for reconsideration), the HRET does not acquire jurisdiction and the House must recognize the candidate COMELEC declares. A second-placer is not automatically the winner.
f: COMELEC’s Second Division disqualified the winner (Codilla) without hearing and proclaimed the second placer (Locsin), who assumed office while Codilla’s reconsideration was pending.
h: Locsin’s proclamation was void; the Speaker was ordered to recognize Codilla.
x: Pending COMELEC case at proclamation: no HRET jurisdiction yet.

r: Where COMELEC cancelled a candidate’s COC before the election and the cancellation became final, the candidate was never validly a candidate; the HRET has no jurisdiction, and swearing in the rightful winner is a ministerial duty of the Speaker and Secretary-General.
f: After Reyes’s COC was finally cancelled, the House kept recognizing her; Velasco sought to be sworn in as Marinduque’s representative.
h: Mandamus granted; Velasco to be administered the oath and registered.
x: Ministerial duties of House officers in carrying out final COMELEC and Supreme Court rulings.

r: The HRET rule requiring at least one Justice for a quorum is valid: the Justices were included to temper partisanship, and only a Justice can chair. Party-list members seeking HRET seats must first go to the House.
f: Regina Reyes challenged the HRET’s 2015 rules, including the quorum rule requiring a Justice, while quo warranto cases against her were pending.
x: Composition and quorum of the tribunals.

r: Each chamber elects its HRET and CA members under the proportional representation rule. Party-list representatives who claim seats must first seek relief from the House; the Court intervenes only if the House fails to comply with the Constitution.
f: Party-list representatives asked the Court to reconstitute the HRET and CA to include them.
h: Petitions dismissed (premature; no showing the House was asked).
x: Primary recourse to the chamber for composition disputes (compare Drilon v. De Venecia).

r: The HRET may annul election results in an election contest, but its decision must rest on substantial evidence; annulling precincts for ‘terrorism’ without proof is grave abuse. The Court retains certiorari power over the tribunals.
f: After a recount widened the winner’s lead, the HRET annulled results in several precincts for alleged terrorism and unseated him.
h: HRET decision reversed; the winner reinstated.
x: Limits of the tribunals’ ‘sole judge’ power: grave abuse remains reviewable.

r: A chamber may reorganize its contingent in the CA when political alignments permanently change (e.g., a new party formed by mass transfers); the change must be permanent, not a temporary alliance. The LDP need not prove a track record to be counted.
f: When the LDP was formed and gained a majority, the House gave it an additional CA seat and removed Daza (Liberal Party).
x: Party-switching and recomposition of the CA or tribunals.

r: Being in the minority does not entitle a member to a CA seat; a party must have enough members for proportional representation. A one-member party in the House was not entitled to a seat.
f: The lone member of KAIBA asked for a CA seat as a minority representative.
x: Proportional representation is computed per party, not per bloc.

r: A senator who does not allege that she or her party was deprived of a CA seat has no standing. Under primary jurisdiction, claims about a chamber’s CA contingent must first be raised in that chamber.
f: Senators questioned the composition of the House contingent in the CA, which had no Liberal Party members.
x: Standing and prior resort in composition disputes.

r: Proportional representation in the CA is mandatory: fractional shares cannot be rounded up at the expense of other parties. The CA can function with fewer than 12 senators as long as it has a majority of its membership.
f: The Senate gave the LDP 8 seats (from 7.5) and a lone-senator party 1 seat (from 0.5).
h: Elections of the extra members (Romulo, Tañada) were void.
test: Senate seats in the CA = (party’s senators ÷ 24) × 12. Fractions are not rounded up if it reduces another party’s share.
